material_dependency_test.basis: The V.B.1 assessment supplies a selected improvement, explicit constraints, available owners, known risks, and verification context. Constructing the bounded implementation plan therefore does not require first executing the separate IV.C.2 root-cause-analysis capability.

dispositions.rationale: Root-cause analysis may inform which improvement is selected, but the implementation target begins after a selected improvement is supplied. The hard prerequisite would encode upstream workflow chronology rather than capability dependence.

material_dependency_test.basis: The V.C.3 assessment supplies a bounded improvement opportunity with explicit scope, constraints, urgency, available participants, and evidence limits. Applying Kaizen or Kaizen-blitz selection does not require first performing the separate V.C.1 waste-elimination analysis target.

dispositions.rationale: Waste elimination can motivate a Kaizen activity, but the qualified Kaizen target is independently executable from its supplied improvement context. No mandatory hard prerequisite is established.

material_dependency_test.basis: The V.C.3 target supplies the improvement opportunity, urgency, scope, constraints, participants, and evidence limits needed to select and structure a Kaizen response. Cycle-time-reduction analysis under V.C.2 is not required to perform that bounded task.

dispositions.rationale: Cycle-time reduction may be one Kaizen objective, but topic relationship and common improvement workflow do not prove a mandatory capability prerequisite. The hard edge is rejected.

Basic SPC concepts plausibly provide conceptual grounding for rational subgrouping, while the VI.A.2 target directly supplies a process and sampling context with timing, grouping options, and constraints. Current machine evidence does not prove whether VI.A.1 must be separately completed first or can be embedded in subgrouping instruction, so the relationship remains noncanonical.

material_dependency_test.basis: The VI.A.3 assessment explicitly supplies variable or attribute data context, the sampling structure, and bounded control-chart evidence. Selecting and interpreting the chart family therefore does not require the learner to first design the subgrouping approach under VI.A.2.

dispositions.rationale: Subgroup structure affects chart choice, but the qualified chart target supplies that structure as input. The separate subgroup-design capability is useful background rather than a proven mandatory prerequisite for this bounded task.
